analysis:
Integration of 8 units. The PR changes only CI plumbing, docs and CI tests: .github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml, .github/workflows/ci.yml, docs-impact.yml, docs/developer/build.md, a changelog entry, scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py and scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py. No provider runtime, coordinator protocol, attestation, App Attest, key custody or prefix-cache code changed. T-041 covers the runtime SSD prefix cache, not CI caches, and TB-002/003/007/009/011 are untouched.

Security-relevant behavior is a net hardening. SAVE_CACHES is true only for push events on master or dev. Every actions/cache/save step in the composite action is gated on inputs.save-caches (action.yml patch hunks at 36-140). Pull requests, including untrusted code, restore caches but no longer write them, which removes the base-side path where a PR could save when nothing matched. Checkouts use persist-credentials: false, so the job token is not stored in the cached .git/config. Cache and checkout actions stay pinned to commit SHAs. The tests in scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py assert no secrets and no continue-on-error on the relevant jobs.

Residual trust assumptions, not findings. A restored .git is validated only by git rev-parse and git fsck --connectivity-only. These do not check .git/config or hooks, so a compromised master or dev push could seed a bad .git for later runs. That needs an already-trusted-branch compromise, so it is not a regression. The scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py change relaxes a substring assertion to a line-anchored regex. It still catches job-level `if:` and allows step-level conditions. The sparse checkout skips only docs/reports/**/*.gz and landing mp4 files. Docs Impact uses blob:none and sparse checkout on the PR head, and I saw no weakened check.

Unverified. The ci.yml head lines 1-540 were only partly visible across units. The remainder was seen in the unit 2 text and the unit 1 base text. Replay source covered 35 of 60 units, so 25 were omitted. The darkbloom-route sandbox runner cache trust is described only in docs, and its workflow was not supplied. The security conclusion does not depend on any of these.
